requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute to MessagePack.Annotations. It has an optional `SurrogateType` property. The source generator finds partial classes marked with it that implement `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, builds an object model for `T`, writes the formatter body into the user's partial class, and registers it in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. There are two modes. Without a surrogate, contractless mode serializes public read-write members under string keys. With a surrogate, the surrogate's `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` attributes are matched to `T` by member name and type. Four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019-022) cover misuse. The change also adds a test-only ExternalTypes assembly with no MessagePack reference, execution tests, generator diagnostic tests, a README section and analyzer docs.
story.why: REQ-2129 asks for a formatter for a type in a referenced assembly that cannot depend on MessagePack, generated in the consuming project from a partial class marked with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]`. The issue lists three options for supplying keys. The change picks none of them and invents a surrogate type instead.

All four named tests in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/GeneratedMessagePackFormatterTests.cs (line 6) run CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator> and never execute MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.

Claim C17 disputed: The execution tests do not successfully round-trip contractless external types: due to targets.Count - 1 in src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs line 135, ExternalPerson.Label and ExternalPoint.Y are never serialized or deserialized, causing ContractlessClassRoundTrips (line 20), ContractlessClassUsesStringKeysForPublicReadWriteMembers (lines 29 and 32), ContractlessStructRoundTrips (line 51), and MessagePackObjectCanContainExternalTypes (line 83) in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.ExecutionTests/GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests.cs to fail.

Off-by-one: `i < targets.Count - 1` drops the last public read-write member. Contractless formatters silently skip a member: Label on ExternalPerson, Y on ExternalPoint. This is data loss on the wire. ContractlessClassRoundTrips, ContractlessClassUsesStringKeysForPublicReadWriteMembers (expects 0x82) and ContractlessStructRoundTrips should fail.
The NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostic is created without message arguments. If its messageFormat has placeholders, the message is malformed. This path has no test.

Surrogate mode enumerates every non-implicit instance field and property of the surrogate, including private or helper members. Any member without [Key] or [IgnoreMember] fails the whole formatter with MsgPack004. The README says 'only the members it lists are serialized', but members without [Key] are not skipped; they are errors.

IsPartial checks only the formatter class, not its containing types. The MsgPack019 doc says nesting types must also be partial. A nested formatter inside a non-partial type gets generated output that fails to compile, without a targeted diagnostic.

The incremental pipeline value holds ISymbol instances. Symbols differ on every compilation, so caching is defeated. The diagnostics branch at MessagePackGenerator L117-129 runs Collect a second time per formatter on every edit.

Attribute matching uses a ToDisplayString string compare. Excluding these formatters from custom-formatter discovery may also hide them from analyzer checks that use the same list. For example, the analyzer might then flag MsgPack003 on [MessagePackObject] types such as ContainsExternalPerson that hold ExternalPerson. This is unverified.

Explicit IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver detection checks m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations.Length > 0 && (m.Name == "OnBeforeSerialize" || m.Name == "OnAfterDeserialize"), which is always false in Roslyn C# because an explicit interface implementation's IMethodSymbol.Name includes the interface prefix (e.g. MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize). It also fails to inspect base types and conflates needsCastOnBefore with needsCastOnAfter, causing CS1061 compile errors in generated formatters (or boxing bugs on structs).

CreateSurrogateMembers iterates GetInstanceMembers(surrogate), which returns private, protected, and internal fields and properties on the surrogate and its base types (skipping only IsImplicitlyDeclared), so any private field on a surrogate triggers MsgPack003 unless marked [IgnoreMember]; additionally, line 171 accepts negative integer [Key] values (e.g. [Key(-1)]), passing negative array indices into FormatterTemplate and crashing generation or producing invalid C# code.

IsPartial only checks whether the formatter class declaration has the partial keyword and never checks symbol.ContainingType (despite doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md line 26). If the formatter is nested inside a non-partial type, MsgPack019 is not reported and EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces generates partial outer declarations that fail with CS0260; also, MessagePackGenerator.cs line 31 filters node is ClassDeclarationSyntax and silently ignores partial record classes marked with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter].

Collect never validates that the user-declared formatter class itself is non-generic, non-abstract, and accessible from GeneratedMessagePackResolver, and line 66 only checks IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter) rather than accessibility from the generated resolver. A generic formatter class (e.g. MyFormatter<U> : IMessagePackFormatter<ConcreteType>), an abstract partial formatter, or a private nested formatter/target type passes validation and produces uncompilable resolver code (CS0122, CS0144, or CS0305).

SurrogateType is cast using as INamedTypeSymbol, so passing a non-named Type such as typeof(int[]) evaluates to null and silently falls back to contractless mode instead of reporting a diagnostic; unbound generic surrogate types like typeof(MySurrogate<>) are also accepted without validation.

CreateSurrogateMembers does not check whether the formatted type T has C# required properties or fields that are omitted or marked [IgnoreMember] on the surrogate; when any required member of T is excluded, the generated formatter's new T() instantiation fails to compile with CS9035.

MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.Initialize was not updated: it advertises MsgPack019-022 in SupportedDiagnostics without ever reporting them (leaving analyzer-only or SuppressSourceGeneration builds without diagnostics), and it adds no exemption for SurrogateType classes carrying [Key] and [IgnoreMember] without [MessagePackObject] against MsgPack001.
